newsitem.title: USA: Malone may be in on Time Warner.
newsitem.headline: Malone may be in on Time Warner.

text.p: Cable-television mogul John Malone may have found a route into the executive suites of Time Warner's merger with Turner Broadcasting System Inc, a daily newspaper reported on Wednesday.

An article in the Atlanta Journal-Constitution said TBS Chairman Ted Turner may be considering naming New York banker and Malone business associate J. Carter Bacot to the board of the new Time Warner.
U.S. regulators, who were expected to approve the deal this week, have barred Malone from management of the new company, the newspaper said.
Officials for TBS, the Atlanta-based parent of Cable News Network, were not immediately available to comment.

The Federal Trade Commission had been concerned that Malone's participation on the Time Warner board would represent too great a concentration of media power in one company. Malone heads Tele-Communications Inc, the largest U.S. cable operator.

The newspaper said Turner was allowed to name two Time Warner board directors because of his standing as vice chairman and the largest individual shareholder of the new company. He already has named himself.
Malone, who has been a close associate of Turner's for years, holds a 20 percent stake in TBS. That would be converted into a nine percent stake in the new Time Warner if the merger were approved.
Bacot, the 63-year-old chief executive of Bank of New York Co Inc, heads an institution that has been a major lender to media companies for decades, the Journal-Constitution said.
Last year, the newspaper noted, Malone's TCI had $628 million in debt outstanding to Bank of New York.
